question: What should you do with your indicator right after finishing a turn?
options: Cancel it straight away
Leave it on for ten seconds
Switch on hazard lights
Flash your headlights
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 says to cancel signals after your manoeuvre.

question: Why is leaving an indicator on after a roundabout exit risky?
options: Waiting drivers may think you are turning and pull out
It drains the car battery quickly
It makes your brakes stop working
It forces cyclists to speed up
explain: Rule 103 warns that lingering signals can mislead waiting drivers.

question: You want to turn left into the second side road. When should you signal?
options: After passing the first side road
Before the first side road
Only after you have turned
Never signal for side roads
explain: Under Rule 103, signalling before an earlier road misleads waiting traffic.

question: What should you do if you see a car ahead signalling left past a side road?
options: Wait until you are sure they are turning
Pull out straight away without checking
Sound your horn and accelerate
Flash your main beam
explain: Rule 103 reminds drivers not to rely solely on another indicator.

question: After changing lanes on a dual carriageway, when should you cancel your signal?
options: As soon as you are in the new lane
Only at the next roundabout
After driving one mile
Only when traffic slows down
explain: Rule 103 says to cancel your indicator once you change lanes.

question: You are waiting at red lights to turn right. Should you keep your right indicator on?
options: Yes, while waiting to turn at the junction
No, switch it off while stationary
Switch to hazard lights instead
Alternate left and right signals
explain: Under Rule 103, keeping your signal on while waiting helps others.

question: Your indicator does not self-cancel after a gentle bend. What must you do?
options: Cancel it by hand straight away
Wait for the next sharp corner
Drive faster so it cancels
Leave it on until you park
explain: Rule 103 requires cancelling signals manually if they stay on.

question: Does giving an indicator signal give you priority over other road users?
options: No, a signal only shows your intention
Yes, other traffic must stop for you
Yes, on dual carriageways only
Yes, if you signal for five seconds
explain: Highway Code Rule 103 states signals do not give you priority.
